mechanism: Britain's debt from the Seven Years' War led Parliament to impose new taxes and tighter control on the American colonies, provoking resistance.
Enlightenment arguments for natural rights and popular sovereignty, spread through colonial pamphlets and newspapers, gave colonists an ideological case against British rule.
Dissatisfaction with the weak Articles of Confederation led states to adopt the 1787 Constitution, which created the federal government of the United States.
The UN Charter's commitment to human rights provided the post-war framework on which the Convention on the Rights of the Child was later drafted.
The Bolshevik seizure of power built the Soviet state whose forced grain requisitions and collectivization in Ukraine produced the famine.
King Wu's forces defeated the Shang army at Muye, ending Shang rule and establishing the Zhou dynasty.
Expressionists rejected Impressionism's focus on optical light, turning instead to subjective emotion and distorted form.
The Expressionist revolt against conventional form and bourgeois norms in German-speaking cities fed directly into the anti-art ideas of Dada.
Viking invasions destroyed rival kingdoms, pushing Wessex under Alfred and Æthelstan to unify the English kingdoms into one realm.
Renaissance curiosity and advances in navigation and cartography fuelled the Portuguese voyages that built the empire.
Portuguese voyages along the African coast and to India opened the sea routes that launched the Age of Discovery.
Portuguese colonization of Brazil from 1500 established one of the first permanent European settlements in the Americas.
The Peace of Westphalia gave Brandenburg's rulers Eastern Pomerania and other territories, expanding the base of the future Prussian state.
Pepin the Short's 756 donation of conquered Lombard lands to the papacy created the territorial base of the Papal States.
The collapse of Western Roman imperial authority left Italy without protection, letting the papacy grow into the dominant local power.
Wartime radar research produced the magnetron, the high-power microwave source that made microwave cooking practical.
Soviet victory at Stalingrad shifted the war's balance, giving Stalin the military leverage he used to press his demands at Yalta.
Germany's June 1941 invasion drew the Soviet Union into the Allied coalition, making Soviet participation and demands central to Yalta.
The Western Allies' June 1944 Normandy landings opened a second front, shaping the postwar zones of control discussed at Yalta.
Nazi Germany's June 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union opened the Eastern Front, the main land theatre of the war in Europe.
The 1939 Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact gave Germany a free hand in Poland, and Hitler's later decision to break it led to the Eastern Front.
The UN Charter's Chapter VIII authorized regional security arrangements, providing the legal basis for the Organization of American States.
Asturian kings launched Christian counter-offensives from the northern mountains, creating a base from which Reconquista campaigns advanced south.
The Asturian victory at Covadonga is traditionally seen as the opening of Christian resistance that grew into the Reconquista.
Almoravid armies crossed into Iberia in 1086 to halt Alfonso VI's advances, drawing the Almoravid dynasty into the Reconquista's struggle.
Almohad rulers intervened in Iberia to halt Christian advances, sustaining the Reconquista's conflict into the twelfth century.
Alexander the Great's conquests across Persia and Egypt spread Greek rule and culture, and his death in 323 BC left the Hellenistic kingdoms.
The Wars of the Diadochi divided Alexander's empire among rival generals, producing the Ptolemaic, Seleucid and Antigonid kingdoms.
Voltaic cell discoveries gave chemists a steady electric current, enabling Nicholson and Carlisle's 1800 electrolysis of water.
Arab-Israeli hostilities and the Palestinian refugee crisis led Arab states to found the PLO in 1964 as the Palestinian national voice.
The Cuban nationalist insurgency against Spanish rule drove the 1895-98 war of independence that drew the United States into the conflict.
Anglo-French Napoleonic conflict led Britain to impress American sailors and enforce trade restrictions, provoking the U.S. declaration of war.
Weapons from Libyan arsenals and Tuareg fighters returning from Gaddafi's army fed the 2012 rebellion that sparked the Mali War.
The 2011 NATO intervention in Libya hardened Russian and Chinese opposition to Western action, shaping the response to the Syrian civil war.
Hutu militias and refugees who fled into eastern Zaire after the genocide fed the Kivu conflict that became part of the Congo wars.
Abbasid patronage in Baghdad, including the translation movement and the House of Wisdom, created the institutions that drove the Islamic Golden Age.
Umayyad rule established Arabic administration and Muslim-ruled cities across the Middle East, creating the territories where Abbasid scholarship flourished.
Islamic scriptural and legal needs, including Quran interpretation and hadith study, motivated early scholarship in language, law and science.
William Morris's Arts and Crafts movement promoted handcraft and organic ornament, which Art Nouveau designers adopted and transformed.
Art Nouveau's break with historical revival styles helped establish the modernist principle of new forms suited to new materials.
Cubist fragmentation of form pushed Futurist painters such as Boccioni toward dynamic, multi-view compositions.
Industrialization and the new machine age supplied the speed and technology that Futurists celebrated in their manifestos.
Futurist manifesto provocation and performance style influenced the anti-art experiments of Dada in Zurich and Berlin.
The Futurist celebration of speed and machines fed into the streamlined, machine-age imagery of Art Deco.
The 1954 US-backed overthrow of Guatemala's Arbenz government convinced Cuban revolutionaries that reform under US-aligned rule was impossible.
Defeat at Sedan and the 1870-71 Prussian siege left Parisians armed and angry, which sparked the Commune's seizure of power in March 1871.
Napoleon III's capture at Sedan collapsed the Second Empire, leaving a political vacuum that let Parisian radicals seize the city.
Lenin and other Marxists drew on the Paris Commune's model of workers' government when they prepared the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.
The Weimar Republic's progressive cultural policy and state funding enabled the founding of the Bauhaus in Weimar in 1919.
Cubist formal experiments shaped Bauhaus teachers' approach to abstraction and the reduction of visual form to basic elements.
Reaction against Baroque excess and ornament pushed seventeenth-century French and English artists toward classical restraint.
Classicism's revival of classical standards of proportion and order became the foundation of eighteenth-century Neoclassicism.
Romantic writers rejected the classicist rules of form and reason, defining themselves in opposition to classicist norms.
France's 1940 defeat in the Battle of France led to the armistice that established the Vichy regime.
Nazi Germany imposed the 1940 armistice terms that created Vichy as a nominally independent French state under German control.
The 843 Treaty of Verdun split the Carolingian Empire, creating West Francia as the core of what became the Kingdom of France.
Capetian succession disputes and English claims to the French crown triggered the Hundred Years' War, in which the French kingdom fought England.
Napoleon's Brumaire coup of 1799 seized power, and his consulate led to the proclamation of the Empire in 1804.
Revolutionary upheaval destroyed the monarchy and created the conditions in which Napoleon could rise to power.
Napoleon created the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807 from Prussian Polish territories, a direct product of the Empire's expansion.
Napoleon's defeat and the end of the Empire led the victorious powers to convene the Congress of Vienna to redraw Europe.
Napoleonic reorganization of Italy spread nationalist ideas and administrative unity that later fed the movement for unification.
The Turkish invasion of Armenia in late 1920 led to Soviet intervention that installed Soviet rule across the republic.
The Red Army's victory in the Russian Civil War enabled Bolshevik conquest of the Caucasus and the creation of Soviet republics there.
The collapse of the First Republic of Armenia left the country open to Soviet takeover in 1920.
The American Revolution produced an independent United States whose 1787 Constitution created a federal judiciary, including the Supreme Court.
Shays's Rebellion in 1786-87 convinced leaders that the Confederation was too weak, prompting the federal courts created by the Constitution.
The Court's Dred Scott decision of 1857 escalated sectional conflict over slavery, one step toward the American Civil War.
Ottoman suzerainty over Crimea made the khanate a vassal state whose rulers depended on Ottoman backing for their authority.
Advances in computing hardware provided the machines and networks on which TCP/IP was designed and tested.
TCP/IP's standardized transport let Berners-Lee build the World Wide Web on top of the internet.
The civil war after Uthman's murder let Mu'awiya seize the caliphate and establish the Umayyad dynasty in 661.
Conquests of Syria, Egypt and Persia supplied the provinces and wealth that the Umayyad state governed from Damascus.
The Abbasid overthrow of the Umayyads in 750 put the Abbasid Caliphate in their place, ruling from Baghdad.
Umayyad armies conquered most of the Visigothic kingdom from 711, creating the Islamic polity of al-Andalus under Umayyad rule.
The Umayyad conquest of Iberia provoked the Christian campaigns to retake territory that became the Reconquista.
Soviet expansion in Eastern Europe and Cold War rivalry gave Washington strong motives to fund the rebuilding of Western Europe.
Nuremberg's establishment of crimes against humanity and genocide principles helped shape the 1948 Genocide Convention.
